That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:

- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

"""kitty: track shared expenses on group trips and work out who owes whom."""


class KittyError(Exception):
    """A user-facing error: printed as a message, exits with status 1."""
import sys

from kitty.cli import main

sys.exit(main())
"""Command-line interface: python3 -m kitty <command>."""

import argparse
import csv
import datetime
import json
import sys

from kitty import KittyError, ledger, store
from kitty.money import allocate, convert, fmt, parse_amount, parse_positive

FORBIDDEN_IN_NAMES = ",="


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    """An ArgumentParser that exits with status 1 on bad usage."""

    def error(self, message):
        self.print_usage(sys.stderr)
        self.exit(1, f"error: {message}\n")


def emit(value):
    print(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False))


# --- validation helpers -----------------------------------------------------

def parse_currency(text):
    code = text.strip().upper()
    if len(code) != 3 or not code.isalpha() or not code.isascii():
        raise KittyError(f"invalid currency code: {text!r} (expected e.g. EUR)")
    return code


def parse_date(text):
    if text is None:
        return datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    try:
        return datetime.date.fromisoformat(text.strip()).isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid date: {text!r} (expected YYYY-MM-DD)")


def parse_id(text, what):
    try:
        value = int(text)
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what} ID: {text!r}")
    return value


def find_member(data, name):
    """Look up a member, ignoring case; returns the name as it was added."""
    wanted = name.strip().casefold()
    for member in data["members"]:
        if member.casefold() == wanted:
            return member
    raise KittyError(f"unknown member: {name!r}")


def parse_name_list(data, text, option):
    names = []
    for part in text.split(","):
        if not part.strip():
            raise KittyError(f"{option}: empty name in {text!r}")
        name = find_member(data, part)
        if name in names:
            raise KittyError(f"{option}: {name} is listed twice")
        names.append(name)
    return names


def parse_name_values(data, text, option):
    """Parse 'A=30,B=20' into an ordered list of (member, raw value)."""
    pairs = []
    for part in text.split(","):
        name, sep, value = part.partition("=")
        if not sep or not name.strip() or not value.strip():
            raise KittyError(f"{option}: expected NAME=VALUE, got {part!r}")
        name = find_member(data, name)
        if any(name == seen for seen, _ in pairs):
            raise KittyError(f"{option}: {name} is listed twice")
        pairs.append((name, value))
    return pairs


def rate_for(data, currency):
    if currency == data["currency"]:
        return "1"
    if currency not in data["rates"]:
        raise KittyError(
            f"no exchange rate for {currency}; set one with "
            f"'rate set {currency} RATE'")
    return data["rates"][currency]


def take_seq(data):
    seq = data["next_seq"]
    data["next_seq"] += 1
    return seq


# --- commands ---------------------------------------------------------------

def cmd_init(args):
    if store.exists():
        raise KittyError(f"{store.FILENAME} already exists here")
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency)
    store.save(store.new_kitty(currency))
    print(f"Started a new kitty in {currency}.")


def cmd_member_add(args, data):
    name = args.name.strip()
    if not name:
        raise KittyError("member name cannot be empty")
    if any(c in name for c in FORBIDDEN_IN_NAMES) or name.startswith("-"):
        raise KittyError(f"member name cannot contain ',' or '=' or start with '-': {name!r}")
    for member in data["members"]:
        if member.casefold() == name.casefold():
            raise KittyError(f"{member} is already a member")
    data["members"].append(name)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Added {name}.")


def cmd_member_remove(args, data):
    name = find_member(data, args.name)
    if ledger.involves(data, name):
        raise KittyError(
            f"{name} is part of recorded expenses or payments; "
            f"remove those first")
    data["members"].remove(name)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"Removed {name}.")


def cmd_member_list(args, data):
    emit(data["members"])


def split_shares(data, args, amount, base_amount):
    """Work out each person's share of an expense, in the base currency."""
    chosen = [opt for opt in ("among", "exact", "shares", "percent")
              if getattr(args, opt) is not None]
    if len(chosen) > 1:
        raise KittyError("use only one of --among, --exact, --shares, --percent")
    method = chosen[0] if chosen else "equal"

    if method == "equal":
        if not data["members"]:
            raise KittyError("there are no members to split among")
        names = list(data["members"])
        weights = [1] * len(names)
    elif method == "among":
        names = parse_name_list(data, args.among, "--among")
        weights = [1] * len(names)
        method = "equal"
    elif method == "exact":
        pairs = parse_name_values(data, args.exact, "--exact")
        names = [n for n, _ in pairs]
        weights = [parse_amount(v, f"--exact amount for {n}", allow_zero=True)
                   for n, v in pairs]
        if sum(weights) != amount:
            raise KittyError(
                f"--exact amounts add up to {fmt(sum(weights))}, "
                f"but the expense is {fmt(amount)}")
    elif method == "shares":
        pairs = parse_name_values(data, args.shares, "--shares")
        names = [n for n, _ in pairs]
        weights = [parse_positive(v, f"--shares value for {n}") for n, v in pairs]
    else:
        pairs = parse_name_values(data, args.percent, "--percent")
        names = [n for n, _ in pairs]
        weights = [parse_positive(v, f"--percent value for {n}") for n, v in pairs]
        if sum(weights) != 100:
            raise KittyError(f"--percent values add up to {sum(weights)}, not 100")

    parts = allocate(base_amount, weights)
    return method, {name: fmt(part) for name, part in zip(names, parts)}


def cmd_expense_add(args, data):
    payer = find_member(data, args.payer)
    amount = parse_amount(args.amount)
    description = " ".join(args.description).strip()
    if not description:
        raise KittyError("description cannot be empty")
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["currency"]
    date = parse_date(args.date)
    category = (args.category or "other").strip().lower()
    if not category:
        raise KittyError("category cannot be empty")
    rate = rate_for(data, currency)
    base_amount = convert(amount, rate)
    method, shares = split_shares(data, args, amount, base_amount)

    expense_id = data["next_expense_id"]
    data["next_expense_id"] += 1
    data["expenses"].append({
        "id": expense_id,
        "seq": take_seq(data),
        "date": date,
        "payer": payer,
        "description": description,
        "amount": fmt(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": rate,
        "base_amount": fmt(base_amount),
        "category": category,
        "split": method,
        "shares": shares,
    })
    store.save(data)
    print(expense_id)


def cmd_expense_list(args, data):
    emit([
        {key: e[key] for key in ("id", "date", "payer", "description", "amount",
                                 "currency", "base_amount", "category", "shares")}
        for _, e in ledger.events({**data, "payments": []})
    ])


def cmd_expense_remove(args, data):
    expense_id = parse_id(args.id, "expense")
    for expense in data["expenses"]:
        if expense["id"] == expense_id:
            data["expenses"].remove(expense)
            store.save(data)
            print(f"Removed expense {expense_id}.")
            return
    raise KittyError(f"no expense with ID {expense_id}")


def cmd_payment_add(args, data):
    sender = find_member(data, args.sender)
    recipient = find_member(data, args.recipient)
    if sender == recipient:
        raise KittyError("a payment needs two different people")
    amount = parse_amount(args.amount)
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency) if args.currency else data["currency"]
    date = parse_date(args.date)
    rate = rate_for(data, currency)

    payment_id = data["next_payment_id"]
    data["next_payment_id"] += 1
    data["payments"].append({
        "id": payment_id,
        "seq": take_seq(data),
        "date": date,
        "from": sender,
        "to": recipient,
        "amount": fmt(amount),
        "currency": currency,
        "rate": rate,
        "base_amount": fmt(convert(amount, rate)),
    })
    store.save(data)
    print(payment_id)


def cmd_payment_list(args, data):
    emit([
        {key: p[key] for key in ("id", "date", "from", "to", "amount",
                                 "currency", "base_amount")}
        for _, p in ledger.events({**data, "expenses": []})
    ])


def cmd_payment_remove(args, data):
    payment_id = parse_id(args.id, "payment")
    for payment in data["payments"]:
        if payment["id"] == payment_id:
            data["payments"].remove(payment)
            store.save(data)
            print(f"Removed payment {payment_id}.")
            return
    raise KittyError(f"no payment with ID {payment_id}")


def cmd_rate_set(args, data):
    currency = parse_currency(args.currency)
    if currency == data["currency"]:
        raise KittyError(f"{currency} is the base currency; its rate is always 1")
    rate = parse_positive(args.rate, "rate")
    data["rates"][currency] = str(rate)
    store.save(data)
    print(f"1 {currency} = {rate} {data['currency']}")


def cmd_balances(args, data):

"""Calculations over a kitty: balances, settlements, history and reports.

Every expense and payment stores its amounts already converted into the base
currency (at the rate in force when it was recorded), so these functions only
ever add up base-currency cents.
"""

from kitty.money import from_cents, to_cents


def events(data):
    """All expenses and payments in date order, then in the order recorded."""
    items = [("expense", e) for e in data["expenses"]]
    items += [("payment", p) for p in data["payments"]]
    items.sort(key=lambda item: (item[1]["date"], item[1]["seq"]))
    return items


def changes(kind, record):
    """How much one expense or payment moves each person's balance, in cents."""
    delta = {}
    if kind == "expense":
        delta[record["payer"]] = to_cents(record["base_amount"])
        for name, share in record["shares"].items():
            delta[name] = delta.get(name, 0) - to_cents(share)
    else:
        cents = to_cents(record["base_amount"])
        delta[record["from"]] = cents
        delta[record["to"]] = delta.get(record["to"], 0) - cents
    return delta


def balances_cents(data):
    totals = {name: 0 for name in data["members"]}
    for kind, record in events(data):
        for name, cents in changes(kind, record).items():
            totals[name] = totals.get(name, 0) + cents
    return totals


def balances(data):
    return {name: from_cents(c) for name, c in balances_cents(data).items()}


def settle(data):
    """Suggest payments that bring everyone to zero.

    Greedily matches the biggest debtor with the biggest creditor, which needs
    at most one payment fewer than the number of people with a balance.
    """
    order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(data["members"])}
    totals = balances_cents(data)
    creditors = [[c, n] for n, c in totals.items() if c > 0]
    debtors = [[-c, n] for n, c in totals.items() if c < 0]
    payments = []
    while creditors and debtors:
        key = lambda pair: (-pair[0], order.get(pair[1], len(order)))
        creditors.sort(key=key)
        debtors.sort(key=key)
        credit, debt = creditors[0], debtors[0]
        amount = min(credit[0], debt[0])
        payments.append({"from": debt[1], "to": credit[1], "amount": from_cents(amount)})
        credit[0] -= amount
        debt[0] -= amount
        if credit[0] == 0:
            creditors.pop(0)
        if debt[0] == 0:
            debtors.pop(0)
    return payments


def involves(data, name):
    return any(name in changes(kind, record) for kind, record in events(data))


def history(data, name):
    rows = []
    balance = 0
    for kind, record in events(data):
        delta = changes(kind, record)
        if name not in delta:
            continue
        balance += delta[name]
        if kind == "expense":
            description = record["description"]
        elif record["from"] == name:
            description = f"Payment to {record['to']}"
        else:
            description = f"Payment from {record['from']}"
        rows.append({
            "date": record["date"],
            "description": description,
            "change": from_cents(delta[name]),
            "balance": from_cents(balance),
        })
    return rows


def report(data):
    """Each person's share of spending per category (not what they paid)."""
    order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(data["members"])}
    totals = {}
    for expense in data["expenses"]:
        category = totals.setdefault(expense["category"], {})
        for name, share in expense["shares"].items():
            category[name] = category.get(name, 0) + to_cents(share)
    return {
        category: {
            name: from_cents(people[name])
            for name in sorted(people, key=lambda n: order.get(n, len(order)))
        }
        for category, people in sorted(totals.items())
    }
"""Money parsing, formatting and exact splitting.

All money is handled as Decimal and rounded to whole cents. Splits are done in
integer cents so the parts of an expense always add up exactly to its total.
"""

from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation
from fractions import Fraction

from kitty import KittyError

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def _parse_decimal(text, what):
    try:
        value = Decimal(text.strip())
    except (InvalidOperation, AttributeError):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}")
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}")
    return value


def parse_amount(text, what="amount", allow_zero=False):
    """Parse a money amount: non-negative, at most two decimal places."""
    value = _parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value < 0 or (value == 0 and not allow_zero):
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be positive: {text!r}")
    if value != value.quantize(CENT):
        raise KittyError(f"{what} can have at most two decimal places: {text!r}")
    return value.quantize(CENT)


def parse_positive(text, what):
    """Parse a positive number of any precision (rates, shares, percentages)."""
    value = _parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be positive: {text!r}")
    return value


def to_cents(value):
    return int((Decimal(value) * 100).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def from_cents(cents):
    return (Decimal(cents) / 100).quantize(CENT)


def fmt(value):
    """Format money as a string with two decimals (never "-0.00")."""
    value = Decimal(value).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    if value == 0:
        value = Decimal("0.00")
    return f"{value:.2f}"


def convert(amount, rate):
    """Convert an amount into the base currency, rounded to the cent."""
    return (Decimal(amount) * Decimal(rate)).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split `total` into parts proportional to `weights`, in whole cents.

    Each part is rounded down to the cent, then the leftover cents go one each
    to the parts in the order given, so the parts sum exactly to `total`.
    Only parts with a positive weight receive leftover cents.
    """
    cents = to_cents(total)
    fractions = [Fraction(Decimal(w)) for w in weights]
    weight_sum = sum(fractions)
    if weight_sum <= 0:
        raise KittyError("cannot split an amount with no positive weights")
    parts = [int(cents * w / weight_sum) for w in fractions]  # >= 0, so int() floors
    leftover = cents - sum(parts)
    # Each part loses less than a cent to rounding down, so the leftover is
    # always fewer cents than there are parts that lost something.
    for i in [i for i, w in enumerate(fractions) if w > 0][:leftover]:
        parts[i] += 1
    return [from_cents(p) for p in parts]

    return os.path.exists(path)


def load(path=FILENAME):
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise KittyError(f"no {path} here; run 'init CURRENCY' first")
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"{path} is not valid JSON: {e}")
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot read {path}: {e.strerror}")
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("version") != VERSION:
        raise KittyError(f"{path} is not a kitty file this version understands")
    return data


def save(data, path=FILENAME):
    """Write atomically, so an interrupted save never leaves a half-written file."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    try:
        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".tmp")
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
                f.write("\n")
            os.replace(tmp, path)
        except BaseException:
            os.unlink(tmp)
            raise
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot write {path}: {e.strerror}")

        raise KittyError("use only one of --among, --exact, --shares, --percent")

"""Calculations over a kitty: balances, settlements, history and reports.

Every expense and payment stores its amounts already converted into the base
currency (at the rate in force when it was recorded), so these functions only
ever add up base-currency cents.
"""

from kitty.money import from_cents, to_cents


def events(data):
    """All expenses and payments in date order, then in the order recorded."""
    items = [("expense", e) for e in data["expenses"]]
    items += [("payment", p) for p in data["payments"]]
    items.sort(key=lambda item: (item[1]["date"], item[1]["seq"]))
    return items


def changes(kind, record):
    """How much one expense or payment moves each person's balance, in cents."""
    delta = {}
    if kind == "expense":
        delta[record["payer"]] = to_cents(record["base_amount"])
        for name, share in record["shares"].items():
            delta[name] = delta.get(name, 0) - to_cents(share)
    else:
        cents = to_cents(record["base_amount"])
        delta[record["from"]] = cents
        delta[record["to"]] = delta.get(record["to"], 0) - cents
    return delta


def balances_cents(data):
    totals = {name: 0 for name in data["members"]}
    for kind, record in events(data):
        for name, cents in changes(kind, record).items():
            totals[name] = totals.get(name, 0) + cents
    return totals


def balances(data):
    return {name: from_cents(c) for name, c in balances_cents(data).items()}


def settle(data):
    """Suggest payments that bring everyone to zero.

    Greedily matches the biggest debtor with the biggest creditor, which needs
    at most one payment fewer than the number of people with a balance.
    """
    order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(data["members"])}
    totals = balances_cents(data)
    creditors = [[c, n] for n, c in totals.items() if c > 0]
    debtors = [[-c, n] for n, c in totals.items() if c < 0]
    payments = []
    while creditors and debtors:
        key = lambda pair: (-pair[0], order.get(pair[1], len(order)))
        creditors.sort(key=key)
        debtors.sort(key=key)
        credit, debt = creditors[0], debtors[0]
        amount = min(credit[0], debt[0])
        payments.append({"from": debt[1], "to": credit[1], "amount": from_cents(amount)})
        credit[0] -= amount
        debt[0] -= amount
        if credit[0] == 0:
            creditors.pop(0)
        if debt[0] == 0:
            debtors.pop(0)
    return payments


def involves(data, name):
    return any(name in changes(kind, record) for kind, record in events(data))


def history(data, name):
    rows = []
    balance = 0
    for kind, record in events(data):
        delta = changes(kind, record)
        if name not in delta:
            continue
        balance += delta[name]
        if kind == "expense":
            description = record["description"]
        elif record["from"] == name:
            description = f"Payment to {record['to']}"
        else:
            description = f"Payment from {record['from']}"
        rows.append({
            "date": record["date"],
            "description": description,
            "change": from_cents(delta[name]),
            "balance": from_cents(balance),
        })
    return rows


def report(data):
    """Each person's share of spending per category (not what they paid)."""
    order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(data["members"])}
    totals = {}
    for expense in data["expenses"]:
        category = totals.setdefault(expense["category"], {})
        for name, share in expense["shares"].items():
            category[name] = category.get(name, 0) + to_cents(share)
    return {
        category: {
            name: from_cents(people[name])
            for name in sorted(people, key=lambda n: order.get(n, len(order)))
        }
        for category, people in sorted(totals.items())
    }
"""Money parsing, formatting and exact splitting.

All money is handled as Decimal and rounded to whole cents. Splits are done in
integer cents so the parts of an expense always add up exactly to its total.
"""

from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation
from fractions import Fraction

from kitty import KittyError

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def _parse_decimal(text, what):
    try:
        value = Decimal(text.strip())
    except (InvalidOperation, AttributeError):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}")
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}")
    return value


def parse_amount(text, what="amount", allow_zero=False):
    """Parse a money amount: non-negative, at most two decimal places."""
    value = _parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value < 0 or (value == 0 and not allow_zero):
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be positive: {text!r}")
    if value != value.quantize(CENT):
        raise KittyError(f"{what} can have at most two decimal places: {text!r}")
    return value.quantize(CENT)


def parse_positive(text, what):
    """Parse a positive number of any precision (rates, shares, percentages)."""
    value = _parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be positive: {text!r}")
    return value


def to_cents(value):
    return int((Decimal(value) * 100).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def from_cents(cents):
    return (Decimal(cents) / 100).quantize(CENT)


def fmt(value):
    """Format money as a string with two decimals (never "-0.00")."""
    value = Decimal(value).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    if value == 0:
        value = Decimal("0.00")
    return f"{value:.2f}"


def convert(amount, rate):
    """Convert an amount into the base currency, rounded to the cent."""
    return (Decimal(amount) * Decimal(rate)).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split `total` into parts proportional to `weights`, in whole cents.

    Each part is rounded down to the cent, then the leftover cents go one each
    to the parts in the order given, so the parts sum exactly to `total`.
    Only parts with a positive weight receive leftover cents.
    """
    cents = to_cents(total)
    fractions = [Fraction(Decimal(w)) for w in weights]
    weight_sum = sum(fractions)
    if weight_sum <= 0:
        raise KittyError("cannot split an amount with no positive weights")
    parts = [int(cents * w / weight_sum) for w in fractions]  # >= 0, so int() floors
    leftover = cents - sum(parts)
    # Each part loses less than a cent to rounding down, so the leftover is
    # always fewer cents than there are parts that lost something.
    for i in [i for i, w in enumerate(fractions) if w > 0][:leftover]:
        parts[i] += 1
    return [from_cents(p) for p in parts]

FILENAME = "kitty.json"

def new_kitty(currency):
    return {

        "currency": currency,

        "expenses": [],
        "payments": [],
        "next_expense_id": 1,
        "next_payment_id": 1,

        # order they were recorded in.
        "next_seq": 1,
    }


def exists(path=FILENAME):
    return os.path.exists(path)


def load(path=FILENAME):
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise KittyError(f"no {path} here; run 'init CURRENCY' first")
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"{path} is not valid JSON: {e}")
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot read {path}: {e.strerror}")
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("version") != VERSION:
        raise KittyError(f"{path} is not a kitty file this version understands")
    return data


def save(data, path=FILENAME):
    """Write atomically, so an interrupted save never leaves a half-written file."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    try:
        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".tmp")
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
                f.write("\n")
            os.replace(tmp, path)
        except BaseException:
            os.unlink(tmp)
            raise
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot write {path}: {e.strerror}")

FORBIDDEN_IN_NAMES = ",="


class Parser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    """An ArgumentParser that exits with status 1 on bad usage."""

    def error(self, message):
        self.print_usage(sys.stderr)
        self.exit(1, f"error: {message}\n")


def emit(value):

# --- validation helpers -----------------------------------------------------

def parse_currency(text):
    code = text.strip().upper()
    if len(code) != 3 or not code.isalpha() or not code.isascii():
        raise KittyError(f"invalid currency code: {text!r} (expected e.g. EUR)")
    return code


def parse_date(text):
    if text is None:
        return datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    try:
        return datetime.date.fromisoformat(text.strip()).isoformat()
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid date: {text!r} (expected YYYY-MM-DD)")


def parse_id(text, what):
    try:
        value = int(text)
    except ValueError:
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what} ID: {text!r}")
    return value


def find_member(data, name):
    """Look up a member, ignoring case; returns the name as it was added."""
    wanted = name.strip().casefold()
    for member in data["members"]:
        if member.casefold() == wanted:
            return member
    raise KittyError(f"unknown member: {name!r}")


def parse_name_list(data, text, option):
    names = []
    for part in text.split(","):
        if not part.strip():
            raise KittyError(f"{option}: empty name in {text!r}")
        name = find_member(data, part)
        if name in names:
            raise KittyError(f"{option}: {name} is listed twice")
        names.append(name)
    return names


def parse_name_values(data, text, option):
    """Parse 'A=30,B=20' into an ordered list of (member, raw value)."""
    pairs = []
    for part in text.split(","):
        name, sep, value = part.partition("=")
        if not sep or not name.strip() or not value.strip():
            raise KittyError(f"{option}: expected NAME=VALUE, got {part!r}")
        name = find_member(data, name)
        if any(name == seen for seen, _ in pairs):
            raise KittyError(f"{option}: {name} is listed twice")
        pairs.append((name, value))
    return pairs


def rate_for(data, currency):
    if currency == data["currency"]:
        return "1"
    if currency not in data["rates"]:
        raise KittyError(
            f"no exchange rate for {currency}; set one with "
            f"'rate set {currency} RATE'")
    return data["rates"][currency]


def take_seq(data):
    seq = data["next_seq"]
    data["next_seq"] += 1
    return seq

        raise KittyError(f"{store.FILENAME} already exists here")

        raise KittyError(f"member name cannot contain ',' or '=' or start with '-': {name!r}")
    for member in data["members"]:
        if member.casefold() == name.casefold():
            raise KittyError(f"{member} is already a member")
    data["members"].append(name)

    print(f"Added {name}.")

    """Work out each person's share of an expense, in the base currency."""
    chosen = [opt for opt in ("among", "exact", "shares", "percent")
              if getattr(args, opt) is not None]
    if len(chosen) > 1:
        raise KittyError("use only one of --among, --exact, --shares, --percent")
    method = chosen[0] if chosen else "equal"

    if method == "equal":
        if not data["members"]:
            raise KittyError("there are no members to split among")
        names = list(data["members"])
        weights = [1] * len(names)
    elif method == "among":
        names = parse_name_list(data, args.among, "--among")
        weights = [1] * len(names)
        method = "equal"
    elif method == "exact":
        pairs = parse_name_values(data, args.exact, "--exact")
        names = [n for n, _ in pairs]
        weights = [parse_amount(v, f"--exact amount for {n}", allow_zero=True)
                   for n, v in pairs]
        if sum(weights) != amount:
            raise KittyError(
                f"--exact amounts add up to {fmt(sum(weights))}, "
                f"but the expense is {fmt(amount)}")
    elif method == "shares":
        pairs = parse_name_values(data, args.shares, "--shares")
        names = [n for n, _ in pairs]
        weights = [parse_positive(v, f"--shares value for {n}") for n, v in pairs]
    else:
        pairs = parse_name_values(data, args.percent, "--percent")
        names = [n for n, _ in pairs]
        weights = [parse_positive(v, f"--percent value for {n}") for n, v in pairs]
        if sum(weights) != 100:
            raise KittyError(f"--percent values add up to {sum(weights)}, not 100")

    parts = allocate(base_amount, weights)
    return method, {name: fmt(part) for name, part in zip(names, parts)}

currency (at the rate in force when it was recorded), so these functions only
ever add up base-currency cents.

from kitty.money import from_cents, to_cents


def events(data):
    """All expenses and payments in date order, then in the order recorded."""
    items = [("expense", e) for e in data["expenses"]]
    items += [("payment", p) for p in data["payments"]]
    items.sort(key=lambda item: (item[1]["date"], item[1]["seq"]))
    return items


def changes(kind, record):
    """How much one expense or payment moves each person's balance, in cents."""
    delta = {}
    if kind == "expense":
        delta[record["payer"]] = to_cents(record["base_amount"])
        for name, share in record["shares"].items():
            delta[name] = delta.get(name, 0) - to_cents(share)
    else:
        cents = to_cents(record["base_amount"])
        delta[record["from"]] = cents
        delta[record["to"]] = delta.get(record["to"], 0) - cents
    return delta


def balances_cents(data):
    totals = {name: 0 for name in data["members"]}
    for kind, record in events(data):
        for name, cents in changes(kind, record).items():
            totals[name] = totals.get(name, 0) + cents
    return totals


def balances(data):
    return {name: from_cents(c) for name, c in balances_cents(data).items()}


def settle(data):
    """Suggest payments that bring everyone to zero.

    Greedily matches the biggest debtor with the biggest creditor, which needs
    at most one payment fewer than the number of people with a balance.
    """
    order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(data["members"])}
    totals = balances_cents(data)
    creditors = [[c, n] for n, c in totals.items() if c > 0]
    debtors = [[-c, n] for n, c in totals.items() if c < 0]
    payments = []
    while creditors and debtors:
        key = lambda pair: (-pair[0], order.get(pair[1], len(order)))
        creditors.sort(key=key)
        debtors.sort(key=key)
        credit, debt = creditors[0], debtors[0]
        amount = min(credit[0], debt[0])
        payments.append({"from": debt[1], "to": credit[1], "amount": from_cents(amount)})
        credit[0] -= amount
        debt[0] -= amount
        if credit[0] == 0:
            creditors.pop(0)
        if debt[0] == 0:
            debtors.pop(0)
    return payments


def involves(data, name):
    return any(name in changes(kind, record) for kind, record in events(data))

    rows = []
    balance = 0
    for kind, record in events(data):
        delta = changes(kind, record)
        if name not in delta:
            continue
        balance += delta[name]
        if kind == "expense":
            description = record["description"]
        elif record["from"] == name:
            description = f"Payment to {record['to']}"
        else:
            description = f"Payment from {record['from']}"
        rows.append({
            "date": record["date"],
            "description": description,
            "change": from_cents(delta[name]),
            "balance": from_cents(balance),
        })
    return rows

    totals = {}
    for expense in data["expenses"]:
        category = totals.setdefault(expense["category"], {})
        for name, share in expense["shares"].items():
            category[name] = category.get(name, 0) + to_cents(share)
    return {
        category: {
            name: from_cents(people[name])
            for name in sorted(people, key=lambda n: order.get(n, len(order)))
        }
        for category, people in sorted(totals.items())
    }
"""Money parsing, formatting and exact splitting.

All money is handled as Decimal and rounded to whole cents. Splits are done in
integer cents so the parts of an expense always add up exactly to its total.
"""

from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation
from fractions import Fraction

from kitty import KittyError

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def _parse_decimal(text, what):
    try:
        value = Decimal(text.strip())
    except (InvalidOperation, AttributeError):
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}")
    if not value.is_finite():
        raise KittyError(f"invalid {what}: {text!r}")
    return value


def parse_amount(text, what="amount", allow_zero=False):
    """Parse a money amount: non-negative, at most two decimal places."""
    value = _parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value < 0 or (value == 0 and not allow_zero):
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be positive: {text!r}")
    if value != value.quantize(CENT):
        raise KittyError(f"{what} can have at most two decimal places: {text!r}")
    return value.quantize(CENT)


def parse_positive(text, what):
    """Parse a positive number of any precision (rates, shares, percentages)."""
    value = _parse_decimal(text, what)
    if value <= 0:
        raise KittyError(f"{what} must be positive: {text!r}")
    return value


def to_cents(value):
    return int((Decimal(value) * 100).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def from_cents(cents):
    return (Decimal(cents) / 100).quantize(CENT)


def fmt(value):
    """Format money as a string with two decimals (never "-0.00")."""
    value = Decimal(value).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    if value == 0:
        value = Decimal("0.00")
    return f"{value:.2f}"


def convert(amount, rate):
    """Convert an amount into the base currency, rounded to the cent."""
    return (Decimal(amount) * Decimal(rate)).quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)


def allocate(total, weights):
    """Split `total` into parts proportional to `weights`, in whole cents.

    Each part is rounded down to the cent, then the leftover cents go one each
    to the parts in the order given, so the parts sum exactly to `total`.
    Only parts with a positive weight receive leftover cents.
    """
    cents = to_cents(total)
    fractions = [Fraction(Decimal(w)) for w in weights]
    weight_sum = sum(fractions)
    if weight_sum <= 0:
        raise KittyError("cannot split an amount with no positive weights")
    parts = [int(cents * w / weight_sum) for w in fractions]  # >= 0, so int() floors
    leftover = cents - sum(parts)
    # Each part loses less than a cent to rounding down, so the leftover is
    # always fewer cents than there are parts that lost something.
    for i in [i for i, w in enumerate(fractions) if w > 0][:leftover]:
        parts[i] += 1
    return [from_cents(p) for p in parts]

    }


def exists(path=FILENAME):
    return os.path.exists(path)


def load(path=FILENAME):
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        raise KittyError(f"no {path} here; run 'init CURRENCY' first")
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"{path} is not valid JSON: {e}")
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot read {path}: {e.strerror}")
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or data.get("version") != VERSION:
        raise KittyError(f"{path} is not a kitty file this version understands")
    return data


def save(data, path=FILENAME):
    """Write atomically, so an interrupted save never leaves a half-written file."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    try:
        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".kitty-", suffix=".tmp")
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
                f.write("\n")
            os.replace(tmp, path)
        except BaseException:
            os.unlink(tmp)
            raise
    except OSError as e:
        raise KittyError(f"cannot write {path}: {e.strerror}")

I've added `expense edit ID` and `--in CUR` for `balances` and `settle`. All 24 tests pass: the 15 existing ones plus 9 new ones I wrote for these features. I also tried both commands by hand.

**`expense edit ID`** (in `kitty/cli.py`)
- It accepts every option you listed and changes only what you pass. The expense keeps its ID and its place among expenses on the same date.
- **Amount or currency changes without a split option:** it's split equally among the same people as before. That applies even if it was split with `--exact` or `--shares` before.
- **Amount changes but the currency doesn't:** the expense keeps the rate it was recorded at, so changing an old USD expense's amount doesn't pick up today's rate. Only a new currency is converted at its current rate.
- **"Changes" means a different value.** Passing the same amount (`10` vs `10.00`) or the same currency leaves the current split alone.
- **A split option without an amount change:** it re-splits the current amount, and `--exact` has to add up to it.
- **Errors** include a bad ID, an unknown member, a currency with no rate, `--exact` amounts that don't add up, or two split options. Any of these leaves the expense untouched.
- It prints `Updated expense N.`, like `expense remove` does.

**`--in CUR` on `balances` and `settle`**
- Each amount is converted from the base currency at the current rate and rounded to the cent, in the same JSON as now.
- `--in EUR` (the base currency) gives the usual amounts. A currency with no rate, or an invalid code, is an error.
- Settle still works out the payments in the base currency and only converts them for display.
- Because each amount is rounded on its own, converted balances may not add up to exactly zero.

**Decisions for you**
- I made `expense edit ID` with no options an error ("nothing to change"). If you'd rather it do nothing and succeed, that's a one-line change.
- `--description` takes several words without quotes, like `expense add` does.

**Other code changes**
